subjects.context: [The user wants research published after a grilling question to appear after that question, before subsequent questions. A Flow contains skill runs called Stages. Each Stage currently has its own tab. The main reading order across Stages is still undecided. This decision unblocks the layout design. No reader code has changed yet.]
subjects.request: Prepare and publish the next question with its Decision brief. Should creation order be the main reading order across the whole Flow or only inside each Stage?

options.label: A. One chronological reading stream across the Flow
options.does: Make creation order across all Stages the main reading experience, with Stage identity retained on content.
gains: A grilling question, later research, and subsequent questions can be read in the order they appeared.
costs: The redesign must provide orientation and filtering without depending on separate Stage tabs as the only reading path.

options.label: B. Keep Stage tabs, order each Stage chronologically
options.does: Keep each skill run as its own reading tab and interleave its Results and questions by creation order.
gains: The present Stage separation remains familiar.
costs: A research Stage between grilling rounds still requires switching tabs to follow the full sequence.

subjects.context: [The main Flow reading path will follow publication order across Stages. Earlier questions can receive answers after later research Results appear. A Result can also be revised later. The behavior of these updates is undecided. This decision unblocks the reader update design. The same underlying data can support either view.]
subjects.request: Prepare and publish the next question with its Decision brief. When earlier content is answered or revised, should the update create a new chronological entry?

options.label: A. Update the original block in place
options.does: Keep answers with their questions and the latest Result at its original creation position, with accessible revision history.
gains: The page stays concise and avoids repeating content.
costs: Creation order is not a complete activity history; readers may not notice a later update far above their position.

options.label: B. Add a linked update entry at the later position
options.does: Retain the original block and append a concise answer or revision event where the update happened.
gains: The sequence explains when a later decision or correction became available.
costs: The reader must distinguish original content from update notices; full content should not be duplicated.

subjects.context: [An interview is underway about rebuilding the Flow reader with Nuxt. The user wrote "vite+" without defining the trailing plus. No tooling integration decision has been made. Confirming the term lets the team choose an integration. No packages have changed.]
subjects.request: Prepare and publish the next question with its Decision brief. Does "vite+" mean the Vite+ product or ordinary Vite?

options.label: A. The Vite+ product
options.does: Treat the separately named Vite+ toolchain as part of the proposal.
gains: The interview will evaluate the integration and what you want from that toolchain.
costs: Compatibility and distribution implications need evidence before accepting it.

options.label: B. Ordinary Vite
options.does: Treat Vite as the intended frontend build tooling, not a request for Vite+.
gains: The interview stays focused on Nuxt without adding a separate toolchain requirement.
costs: No capabilities specific to Vite+ are requested.

subjects.context: [The user wants a Nuxt Flow reader with chronological reading across Stages. Typography, density, and the broader visual design have not been agreed. Implementation has not started. The next step is either a prototype for review or implementation using the agreed reading order. Neither step has started.]
subjects.request: Prepare and publish the next question with its Decision brief. Should the broader visual design be reviewed as a prototype before implementation?

options.label: A. Review a prototype first
options.does: Use the agreed reading sequence to propose a visual design, then review that design before production implementation.
gains: You can judge the actual reading experience rather than approve an abstract framework choice.
costs: The exact appearance remains a separate design decision until that review.

options.label: B. Use the current visual style for this change
options.does: Preserve the current visual language while implementing chronological reading and the Nuxt migration.
gains: The work has a narrower and more concrete design target.
costs: A broader visual restyling is intentionally excluded rather than implicitly designed by the framework.
